title: Qiskit Runtime — Hybrid Execution Model
description: Qiskit Runtime is IBM's execution model for the quantum-classical loop: instead of queueing every circuit separately, the classical optimizer runs co-located with the QPU and streams circuits with sub-second latency. Primitives like Sampler and Estimator replaced raw job submission, cutting variational workloads from hours to minutes. It is the closest thing the field has to a quantum operating system's process model.

title: ARTIQ and Sinara — Open Quantum Control Hardware

title: Pulse-Level Programming — Qiskit Pulse

It is the difference between driving an automatic and opening the gearbox.

title: Transpiler Optimization Levels
description: The transpiler is the quantum compiler pass that rewrites abstract circuits onto real hardware: rebasing gates to the native set, routing around limited connectivity with SWAPs, and optimizing away redundancies. Qiskit's levels 0–3 trade compile time for circuit quality; level 3 can halve two-qubit counts on deep circuits. On noisy hardware, transpiler quality is second only to the device itself in determining whether a result means anything.

title: Cloud Queue Schedulers — Fair Share

It is an operating system's process scheduler, stretched across the planet.

title: Error Mitigation as a Service Layer
description: Error mitigation is becoming infrastructure rather than user code: runtime services that automatically apply zero-noise extrapolation, readout correction, and dynamical decoupling around every job. This is the quantum equivalent of the OS memory manager — everyone uses it, nobody hand-rolls it.

title: Cryogenic Control — Cryo-CMOS
description: Every qubit wire running from room temperature to millikelvin carries heat, and thousands of qubits need thousands of wires — the wiring bottleneck. Cryo-CMOS puts control electronics inside the fridge at 4K, multiplexing signals and cutting the wire count by orders of magnitude. Intel's Horse Ridge and academic prototypes prove the concept; scaling it is one of the field's critical engineering races.

This record tracks the proposals, not a product: the OS layer is the stack's biggest open gap.

title: Distributed Quantum Stack — Entanglement Distribution
description: Distributed quantum computing links processors with entanglement: photons carry Bell pairs between nodes, repeaters extend the range, and teleportation moves data without moving qubits. Delft, Chicago, and Hefei run the testbeds; a quantum internet is infrastructure decades in the making.
